_readThisFirst.warning: SoifGo does NOT use REST/HTTP APIs inside the WebView.
_readThisFirst.howItWorks: HTML page calls CallSub() → SoifGo app sends via Bluetooth/MQTT → hardware responds → SoifGo app calls your JS callback function.

_forAIAssistants.step1: Read the 'bridge' section to understand how to call SoifGo functions.
_forAIAssistants.step2: Use the EXACT Sub names listed in 'bluetooth' and 'sensors' sections.
_forAIAssistants.step3: Never invent function names. Never use fetch().
_forAIAssistants.step4: Always attach callbacks to window.* (e.g. window.html_bluetooth_tx = ...).

bridge.simpleExplanation: This is the ONLY way to talk to hardware from HTML in SoifGo.

subName.description: The exact Sub name (case-sensitive) — see list below

args.description: Arguments to pass (usually a string command)

bridge.availability: window.soifgo ONLY exists inside SoifGo's WebView. Guard with: if (window.soifgo) { ... }

send.whatItDoes: Send a text command to the connected Bluetooth device (HC-05, ESP32, etc.)
send.important: The name 'html_bluetooth_rx' looks backwards but is the ACTUAL Sub name. Do not change it.

receive.whatItDoes: Receive data sent from the Bluetooth device back to your HTML page
receive.important: You MUST attach the function to window, otherwise SoifGo cannot find it.

light.whatItDoes: Stream ambient light sensor data from the phone

motion.whatItDoes: Stream accelerometer (motion) data from the phone

_rulesForAI: ❌ DO NOT use fetch() — it will not work inside SoifGo WebView
❌ DO NOT use XMLHttpRequest, axios, or any HTTP library
❌ DO NOT invent function names like 'sendBluetooth' or 'controlLed'
❌ DO NOT create REST endpoints (/api/led/on, etc.) — they do not exist
✅ DO attach callbacks to window: window.html_bluetooth_tx = html_bluetooth_tx
✅ DO guard all calls with: if (window.soifgo) { ... }
✅ DO use the EXACT case-sensitive Sub names listed above
